Second, the instrument's central claim, verified by reading the code rather than the prose: `_MANIFEST_GENERABILITY_MECHANISMS` declares `waived` at export.py:2457, `_manifest_source_mechanism` maps it at 2476-2477, `generable` is `all(entry['mechanism'] == 'waived')` at 2541 -- and the export leg's only disposition assignments are `documented_non_nameable` (3281), `emitted` (3284) and `excluded` (3287), with no fourth branch, exactly as the record says. `grep -rn waived` over imas_codec/ names it only in export.py; the manifest row schema carries exactly five keys (`source_path`, `source_status`, `standard_name_id`, `terminal_stage`, `non_nameable_reason`) and no disposition key, so the channel claim holds as well. Third, the baseline comparison, which I re-derived independently: classifying the embedded manifest by the same rules reproduces `{recorded_refusal: 21, composition_not_scheduled: 4}` and 25 uncarried, so the recorded baseline and the ten-source movement are identity-level accurate. Point TWO of the brief is answered by that third check: a repair reported as landed on the strength of a declared vocabulary member is exactly what this node overturns, and the overturn is correct -- the successor-chain walk is read-only (`MATCH`/`RETURN` only; the function spans graph_ops.py:12893-13004 and the successor statement sits at 12957-12959, seeded by `start.id IN $seed_ids`), the vocabulary member exists, the producer does not. A fourth check, on coverage rather than correctness: an identity absent from the graph is fail-visible in this instrument, not invisible -- an absent `StandardNameSource` returns no reason, `fetch_manifest_source_release_rows` therefore writes the `cause not recorded` sentinel, and `_manifest_source_mechanism` returns `composition_not_scheduled` for it (2488-2489) -- and the live read reports ZERO of that class, so none of the 355 rows is an absent-node artifact and the 340/15 split describes identities the graph actually holds. Whatever the 67 identities absent elsewhere in the graph may be, they are not load-bearing for this measurement, and the run's own record says as much by reporting `live_rows_returned 355` against `manifest_source_paths 355`. Deductions: the `attempt_budget_exhausted` citation is four lines off (finding 1); the uniform mechanism column is answered structurally rather than by a positive control in THIS run -- the node never shows its instrument emitting a non-`recorded_refusal` mechanism, which I supplied from the suite (tests/standard_names/test_manifest_generability.py:299-343 constructs a `waived` record and asserts `mechanism_counts == {'waived': 1}`, so the check does see a waiver when one is present); and the doc's final sentence, that the instrument is deterministic so a re-run reproduces the counts, is asserted without a second run, which is the one claim in the record that a cheap control could have carried and did not.

It did exactly that and answered the harder question underneath it. `verdict.json` on disk gives manifest_size 355, carried 340, uncarried 15, generable False, all_gates_passed False, gate_failures 1 on `manifest_generability` alone, mechanism_counts {'recorded_refusal': 15}, exported_count 230 -- and the printed log lines at the tail of run.log carry the same values, so the numbers are read from a receipt rather than reported from memory. Against the recorded baseline the record is honest about both directions: ten recovered, verdict unmoved. Point ONE of the brief: I verified the permanence claim per identity against each row's recorded reason rather than against the column, and the node's own table is right -- twelve of the fifteen are refusals by design (five `dd_node_category_ineligible: fit_artifact` backings and seven time axes: six bare `time` tokens and `equilibrium/time_slice/time`'s nested axis) and three are not (calorimetry/group/component/energy_total/data, `vocab_gap_nonactionable`, owned by the ISN grammar; camera_x_rays/camera/camera_dimensions, `compose claim-attempt cap reached`, a spent budget; equilibrium/time_slice/contour_tree/node/z, `compose_model_skipped`, work nothing has scheduled). So no, the node does not claim all fifteen are permanent, and the two transient ones are transient: each can be reached by finishing work, and the node says so. The claim that survives all fifteen -- the cut cannot become generable by finishing work -- is TRUE, but for a sharper reason than the supervisor's brief assumes: close all three and twelve permanent exclusions still block, and they are unwaivable (finding 1 below). One point deducted because that consequence is stated in the waived section and not attached to the table's 'permanent?' column, so a reader who reads only the table concludes that three more items of work would clear the gate.
justifications.scope_discipline: Exact on every path the fence covers. The four declared write paths are `docs/evidence/unbound-source-backlog/west-gate-chain-verdict.md`, `docs/evidence/archive/unbound-source-backlog-landed.html, and `docs/figures/unbound-source-backlog` (the west-gate-chain.svg) and `docs/plans/unbound-source-backlog.html`; `git show --stat 0dceb0d94` reports exactly those four files, 309 insertions, 0 deletions, and the merge 551ec0bf5 carries the same four with no additional content -- a docs-only node that left every production file alone, which is what the role required. The plan it edited is the plan it lands against, which is the one plan a node may touch. Commits are conventional with a body, no AI attribution, and no plan, sprint or ticket identifier in the message, the paths or the figure's internals. The read-only discipline holds under the check the bounded-read section of this repo demands: `measure_west_generability.py` performs no graph write (its only writes are `verdict.json` and a `TemporaryDirectory`), `export.py` contains no Cypher write verb anywhere (`grep -nE 'session\.run|CREATE |MERGE |SET |DELETE '` over the module returns only `write_text`/`write_bytes` calls), and the cohort read goes through `fetch_manifest_source_release_rows` (graph_ops.py:12893), the release's own projection. Point THREE of the brief: the node wrote nothing to the graph -- from its own record (`No graph write of any kind was performed`, plus the script's shape and the absence of a fourth disposition branch that a write would need) and from the fact that the uncarried set it reports is entirely composed of rows a write would have changed. Two further checks of my own: I scanned the run's own stream (`stream.jsonl`, 3.3 MB) for write verbs -- `CREATE (` 0, `MERGE (` 0, `add_to_graph` 0, `DETACH DELETE` 0, and the single `DELETE` hit is the node's own grep pattern for write verbs inside export.py, i.e. the search text rather than a statement; and the earlier `srun: error ... Exited with code 1/2` lines in that stream are its own first attempts failing before the job that produced the verdict. One precision owed on boundedness: statement 2's rows are successors of the seed identities, not the seeds themselves, so the bullet 'no traversal reaches a node outside the set of identities those paths resolve to' should read 'outside the closure of those identities'; the query table states the walk correctly and the returned row bound (355) is the cohort's own.
